notes:
Account background:
- Mid-market KM SaaS, vertical: B2B professional services (knowledge bases + search)
- Heavy production usage: user-facing summarization + conversational support widget across desktop and mobile
- Currently on OtherProviderAPI (historical spend ~ $3k/month on tokens); evaluating Redwood for cost predictability and lower latency at scale

Discovery highlights:
- Primary ask: migrate from OtherProviderAPI -> Redwood Hosted, then Dedicated once we hit predictable traffic (~200 reqs/s peak).
- Need a compatibility layer to avoid full prompt rewrite; team prefers OpenAI-compatible endpoints. "Don't break prompts" quoted from CTO.
- POC scope: 1) API parity 2) prompt-parity on top 3) latency SLOs 4) cost estimate for dedicated capacity

POC notes (Jan-Feb):
- Redwood Hosted demo 2026-02-11 (Jordan + Priya + product leads). Demo focused on streaming parity and function-calling.
- POC run: ran 1500 prompt pairs (summary + follow-up) through Redwood Hosted and OtherProvider to compare tokens and output differences. See drive:/pocs/verdant/prompt-parity-report.xlsx for raw diffs.
- Results: generated outputs largely equivalent for retrieval-augmented summaries, but two regression patterns flagged:
  * deterministic tokens: slight change in truncation behavior at 2048 tokens -> resulted in missing trailing context for ~2.7% of tests
  * hallucination delta: one prompt family showed higher incorrect entity hallucinations when temperature/profile differed from their tuned OtherProvider model
- Redwood SE suggested compatibility wrapper: map ChatCompletion-style messages, preserve system role, and pin sampling params. Redwood also recommended using Optimize suggestions (quantization + batching) to reduce cost for Dedicated.

Security & compliance:
- Require SOC2 audit report, SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, audit logging for model inputs/outputs, and EU data residency for a subset of customers.
- Legal requested a data residency clause; paused procurement until draft language provided. Linked doc: drive:/security/verdant-shelf/security-answers.docx

Commercials & cost sensitivity:
- Team sensitive to per-token spend. Interested in hybrid pricing: hosted for dev & canary, dedicated for production spikes.
- Wants a clear migration path and migration credits during the first quarter after switch. Discussed estimated ARR band $75k-200k.

Internal stakeholders:
- CTO: Lina Morales (concerned about prompt regressions & latency)
- Head of Product: Amir Shah (owns POC success criteria)
- Platform Eng: Ravi Mahadevan (owns infra & SSO integration)

Quotes & shorthand from calls:
- "If we have to rewrite prompts it's a non-starter." -- CTO
- "Need a safety net: if Redwood output regresses, auto-fallback to OtherProvider for canary traffic." -- Head of Product

Next steps (explicit):
- Redwood to run regression evals with Optimize team using their 10k prompt set (assigned to Priya). Deadline: 2026-03-31.
- Schedule Dedicated capacity sizing call (target week of 2026-03-22). Owner: Jordan.
- Legal to receive draft data-residency clause from Redwood legal; expect review by 2026-04-08.
- SE patch: deliver compatibility wrapper code sample + migration checklist (GH gist link in drive doc).
notes_summary: Mid-market KM SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted->Dedicated. POC shows good parity but two regression classes found (truncation & hallucination delta). Key blockers: budget sign-off, legal data-residency language, and fixing prompt-parity regressions. Next: regression evals, dedicated sizing call, SSO/KMS SOW.
